section_summary: This section documents U.S. inter-agency deliberations and diplomatic coordination between September and November 1947 concerning international grain export allocations and food policy for occupied Japan, Korea, and Europe. It focuses on the contentious dispute between the Department of State and the Department of the Army over Far Eastern Commission paper FEC 248/4, specifically the Army's proposal to expand civilian food relief criteria from preventing 'disease and unrest' to attaining the 'objectives of the occupation.' The controversy was resolved through a State Department compromise limiting the policy to the 1947–1948 Japanese crop year, alongside parallel efforts to arrange advance grain shipments from the Pacific Northwest.

subfiles.about: Analyzes international distribution and deficits of U.S. grain exports under 12-million and 14-million-ton availabilities for 1947–1948.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes international allocations and deficits under 12-million and 14-million-ton U.S. export programs, comparing food needs in Germany, Japan, and Marshall Plan nations.
subfiles.title: U. S. Grain Exports - 1947-48

subfiles.about: Outlines proposed domestic conservation measures and rationing to attain a 14.5-million-ton grain export goal.
keywords: Cabinet Committee on World Food Programs
subfiles.summary: Draft notes on grain conservation methods, livestock feed reductions, and milling adjustments to meet a 14.5-million-ton export target.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Notes on Grain Conservation and Export Targets

subfiles.about: Recommends governmental actions and controls to achieve an export target of 14,500,000 tons of grain during 1947–1948.
keywords: Cabinet Committee on World Food Programs
subfiles.summary: Recommends conservation campaigns, aggressive CCC procurement, tax deferrals, and allocation controls to achieve a 14.5-million-ton grain export goal.
subfiles.title: Wheat Export Program

subfiles.about: Projects non-farm calorie consumption and cereal ration impacts in European countries under alternative U.S. grain export programs.
subfiles.summary: Statistical tables detailing non-farm calorie consumption and cereal ration deficits across European countries under alternative U.S. export programs.
subfiles.title: Tables on Estimated Effects of Alternative U.S. Grain Export Programs on Cereal Rations and Calorie Consumption in Selected European Countries, 1947/48

subfiles.about: Advises against the Department of the Army's proposed amendment inserting 'objectives of the occupation' into the FEC food policy statement.
subfiles.summary: Warns that the Army amendment to FEC 248 would undermine Allied trust, alienate Commission members, and harm U.S. leadership.
subfiles.title: Letter on Department of the Army Amendment to FEC Paper on Civilian Food Supply for Japan

subfiles.about: Recommends instructing the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission to vote for the Japanese food policy paper without the Army's amendment.
subfiles.summary: Recommends directing the U.S. FEC member to approve the Japanese food paper without the Army's 'objectives of the occupation' amendment.
subfiles.title: FEC Policy for Japanese Food Imports

subfiles.about: Proposes directing the U.S. FEC representative to vote for the food policy paper amended to terminate at the end of the current Japanese crop year.
subfiles.summary: Recommends approving the FEC food paper modified to terminate after the 1947–1948 crop year, rejecting the Army's wording.
subfiles.title: FEC Policy for Japanese Food Imports

subfiles.about: Outlines theater and Army food requirements versus projected Department of Agriculture allocations for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.summary: Compares Japan and Korea 'disease and unrest' grain requirements against projected Department of Agriculture export allocations.
subfiles.title: Food Supply for Japan for 1947-1948

subfiles.about: Submits draft letters to the Department of Agriculture and Tracy S. Voorhees supporting advance shipments of grain to Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Transmits draft letters endorsing advance West Coast grain shipments to Japan and Korea within established allocations.
subfiles.title: Preshipment of Grain to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Supports advance shipments of grain from the West Coast to Japan and Korea provided total allocations and European programs are not compromised.
subfiles.summary: Concurs with early grain shipments to Japan and Korea, provided total allocations and European programs are not prejudiced.
subfiles.title: Letter to Jesse Gilmer Concerning Preshipment of Cereals to Pacific Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: Informs Voorhees of State Department support for advance grain shipments to Japan and Korea and encloses the letter to the Department of Agriculture.
subfiles.summary: Confirms agreement to advance grain shipments for Japan and Korea within established limits and encloses letter to USDA.
subfiles.title: Letter to Tracy S. Voorhees Concerning Preshipment of Grain to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Instructs Lewis to assist with the grain preshipment project requested by the Army.
subfiles.summary: Directs staff to assist appropriately with the grain preshipment project with a suspense date of November 10.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning Grain Preshipment Project

subfiles.about: Requests State Department support in obtaining increased advance shipments of grain to Japan and Korea from the Department of Agriculture.
subfiles.summary: Urges State Department support for advance grain shipments to Japan and Korea, enclosing MacArthur's cable and a USDA letter.
subfiles.title: Letter to Charles E. Saltzman Regarding Grain Shipments to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Explains the critical need for scheduled grain imports to Japan and Korea and warns against inadequate winter allocations.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Warns that reduced winter allocations will exhaust stocks and disrupt rationing, urging scheduled shipments to avert economic crisis.
subfiles.title: Telegram C 56240 on Food Import Requirements for Pacific Areas

subfiles.about: Sets forth operational and logistical justifications for advance shipments of grain to Japan and Korea from the West Coast.
subfiles.summary: Urges advance grain shipments from the Pacific Northwest to Japan and Korea to optimize shipping and avert spring famine.
subfiles.title: Letter to Jesse Gilmer Requesting Preshipment of Cereals to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Explains why the Department of State cannot accept the Army's proposed amendment to paragraph 3 of FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Carbon copy requesting the Army withdraw its amendment to FEC 248/4, maintaining that disease and unrest standards suffice.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to William H. Draper, Jr., Regarding FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Relays Linville's suggestion to add text regarding the overly broad interpretation of 'objectives of the occupation' to the draft letter to Draper.
subfiles.summary: Suggests inserting language into the letter to Draper warning that 'objectives of the occupation' is interpreted too broadly.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on Suggested Addition to Letter on FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Transmits the Department of State's formal request that the Department of the Army withdraw its proposed amendment to FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Official letter urging Under Secretary Draper to withdraw the proposed Army amendment to paragraph 3 of FEC 248/4.
subfiles.title: Letter to William H. Draper, Jr., Concerning Proposed Amendment to FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Defends the Department of the Army's insistence on adding 'to attain the objectives of the occupation' to FEC-248/4.
subfiles.summary: Defends the Army's insistence on occupation objectives in FEC-248/4 to ensure food imports adequate for Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.title: Letter Concerning Department of the Army Position on FEC-248/4

subfiles.about: Provides detailed reasons why the Department of State should reject the Army's proposed amendment to FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Argues the Army amendment is unnecessary, violates past commitments, and would provoke strong resentment among Far Eastern Commission Allies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on FEC Policy for Japanese Food Imports

subfiles.about: Alerts NA and FE officers of the urgency of the FEC food paper decision and the need to coordinate with General McCoy and General Draper.
subfiles.summary: Alerts staff to the urgency of the FEC food paper and the need to coordinate with McCoy and Draper.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning the FEC Food Paper

subfiles.about: Directs Claxton to have Whitman prepare a letter to Draper laying out arguments against amending the FEC food paper.
subfiles.summary: Directs preparation of a letter to Draper arguing against amending the FEC food paper and requests the paper.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Routing Notes on FEC Food Paper and Draft Letter to Draper

subfiles.about: Details the policy background of FEC food proposals and recommends vigorously resisting the Army's amendment.
subfiles.summary: Traces FEC food paper history and recommends vigorously resisting the Army amendment to prevent severe diplomatic damage.
subfiles.title: Supply of Food for Civilian Consumption in Japan - FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Draft letter setting forth Department of State objections to amending paragraph 3 of FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter requesting the Department of the Army withdraw its proposed amendment to paragraph 3 of FEC 248/4.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to William H. Draper, Jr., Concerning Proposed Amendment to FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Reports on the dispatch of SWNCC 331 to SCAP and compares provisions of SWNCC 331/3 with FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Notes that SWNCC 331 was sent to SCAP without reply, and SWNCC 331/3 resembles FEC 248/4.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum on Food Imports

subfiles.about: Working draft memorandum analyzing the Army amendment to FEC 248/4 and recommending acceptance without amendment.
subfiles.summary: Annotated draft memorandum advising Under Secretary Lovett to approve the FEC food paper without the Army amendment.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum on FEC Policy for Japanese Food Imports

subfiles.about: Sets forth the Far Eastern Commission's policy decision restricting civilian food imports to Japan during the acute world shortage.
subfiles.summary: Prohibits food imports giving preferential treatment to Japan over Allied populations except as essential for occupation forces' safety.
subfiles.title: Food Supply for Japan (FEC Policy Decision, April 25, 1946)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Compares estimated disease and unrest food requirements for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus against projected Department of Agriculture allocations.
subfiles.summary: Statistical comparison of Pacific occupied area food requirements against projected Department of Agriculture grain export availabilities.
subfiles.title: Food Supply for Japan for 1947-1948

subfiles.about: Presents recommendations and an extensive background annex advocating a crop year limitation rather than the Army amendment for FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman recommends authorizing the U.S. FEC representative to support FEC 248/4 with a one-year crop termination compromise rather than the Army's amendment. The attached annex details diplomatic history, refutes Army arguments regarding economic recovery, highlights Allied sensitivities, and analyzes previous SWNCC directives.
subfiles.title: FEC Policy for Japanese Food Imports (with Annex)

subfiles.about: Routing note referring to an upcoming Army Department memorandum to SCAP concerning early 1948 food shipments.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note concerning an upcoming Army Department memorandum to SCAP regarding January and February 1948 food shipments.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning Upcoming Army Memorandum on Food to SCAP

subfiles.about: Confirms that the Department of the Army withdraws its objection to FEC 248/4 following General McCoy's official statement to the FEC.
subfiles.summary: Informs Wisner that the Army accepts General McCoy's November 20 FEC statement and withdraws objections to FEC 248/4.
subfiles.title: Letter Concerning Department of the Army Acceptance of FEC 248/4

subfiles.about: Announces U.S. approval of FEC 248/4 provided its duration is limited to the 1947–1948 Japanese crop year.
subfiles.summary: Official statement to the FEC approving FEC 248/4 on condition of limiting its application to the 1947–1948 Japanese crop year.
subfiles.title: Statement by General McCoy at the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of General McCoy's statement to the Far Eastern Commission proposing the crop year time limit on FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of General McCoy's statement proposing a 1947–1948 crop year limitation on the FEC Japanese food paper.
subfiles.title: Statement by General McCoy at the Far Eastern Commission (Copy)

subfiles.about: Sets forth tactical procedure and language for General McCoy to follow in the Far Eastern Commission regarding FEC 248/4.
subfiles.summary: Outlines procedural and tactical steps for General McCoy regarding FEC 248/4, including postponement and crop year limitation.
subfiles.title: Procedure for General McCoy to Follow in FEC Regarding FEC 248/4
